Definition: from ἀργός (shining); silver (the metal, in the articles or coin):--silver.
BiblicalUsage: Silver is the metal itself, shining and weighed out as money. The disciples are told to carry no silver in their purses, Paul tells Athens the Godhead is not like gold or silver or stone graven by art, a man's work may be built on gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, or stubble, and James says the rich man's gold and silver is cankered and will eat their flesh like fire.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe silver is honest about itself: it shines, it weighs, and it rusts. What is built on it will be tried by fire, and only what survives the fire was ever worth building.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Paul; James, Brother of Jesus
